proof: Two live runs on the real gateway with the repository's credentials; their recordings replayed through the real adapter on macOS, Linux and Windows; a real Core over the Anthropic protocol; the forge adapter over a real socket; and a gate, run in CI, that holds the declared inventory to the code, the workflows, the fixtures and the retained records of the run that made them.
negative_proof: mutation-1: an adapter that sends a changed prompt_cache_key is refused at /body/prompt_cache_key; mutation-2: a decoder reading the provider id from the wrong field fails on the stream ids; mutation-3: a real skipped live run exits 0 from cargo test and 1 from integration_gate.py --live with four failures; 20 gate cases each fail for exactly one cause (undeclared Rust and TypeScript connections, stale claim, missing test, helper-not-test, no live or component level, unaccepted or missing deferral record, --release on a deferral, a live test no workflow runs, a non-live_ external test, a credential header, a fixture recorded outside CI, a fixture no retained run wrote, an edited fixture, a skipped record, no record, a pass that proved another integration, a real service without its integration level or with an external one).
found_on_the_way: the nightly live proof had been red for four days: the cancellation step cancelled only on a MessageDelta, and glm-5.3-flash now reasons first, spending all 256 tokens counting inside its reasoning; the fix cancels on the first streamed token of either kind and gives the counting request room
the replay server first counted a request as served after writing the stream terminator, but the adapter is done at the last event, so the count raced the assertion; it now counts on acceptance

the first test-detection rule accepted any #[test] within six lines above a function, which let a helper right below a test pass as one; the gate now reads only the attributes directly on the function
limitations: forge.github's real-API level stays deferred by DR-M6-002 until the owner supplies MODBIT_GITHUB_TOKEN and a test repository (docs/77 §5 item 2), so integration_gate.py --release fails on it today — the requirement working, not a gap; no live forge test was written because it could not be run. The live level runs on a compatible gateway (DR-M9-002) and does not discharge docs/15's production-endpoint clause. A fixture's authenticity rests on its sha256 in the retained record of a named CI run, not on a signature. Each recorded answer arrived as one network chunk, so frame splitting is covered by the component suite, not by the recordings. Coverage is detected by source patterns for outbound clients; a connection through a crate not on the list would not be seen.
